title: Capstone: an analytical visualization with an evidence record
outcome: Build a linked numerical, static and interactive analysis whose denominators, identities, uncertainty and delivery limits can be reviewed.
mechanism:
An analytical visualization should connect its displayed marks to an explicit calculation. This capstone begins with identified synthetic records, a declared missing-value policy and two groups. The raw data, summary table and figures remain separate artifacts so a reviewer can reconstruct every value rather than trusting the appearance of a polished chart.

The observed-value policy retains eight measured values and records two missing measurements. Each group has four observed values. Means, standard errors and Student t intervals are calculated from those admitted observations. The intervals target group means under their stated assumptions; they are not predictions for future individuals and do not establish a causal treatment effect.

The static graphic shows observations and the mean intervals together. The interactive figure retains observation IDs and a separate summary trace with error bars. The summary trace does not add new observations to the underlying dataset. Counting all rendered points as sample size would therefore be a denominator error.

A printed table provides an alternative to hover and makes the eligibility counts inspectable. The report should name the metric, missingness rule, interval construction, package environment and limitations. A difference between group means is descriptive here because no randomized or otherwise identified causal design is supplied.

Acceptance proceeds through several evidence layers: numeric assertions, layer/trace parity, explicit plot printing, captured figure structure and actual browser inspection. This reference performs the first stages and can be executed through the prepared worker capture path. It does not infer readable labels, working hover controls or accessibility from a successful Rscript exit.

For independent work, change the group sizes or missingness pattern and derive the new expected summaries before modifying the figures. Explain how the report would change if the target were an overall observation mean, an equal-group mean or a causal contrast. A defensible analysis keeps those questions distinct.

vocabulary.definition: Counts and rules determining which records contribute to a calculation.
Marks representing derived statistics rather than additional raw observations.
The explicit estimator, standard error and critical-value procedure behind an uncertainty display.
A report connecting source data, calculations, rendered payloads and the limits of observed validation.

anatomy: Create a keyed raw data frame, select observed values under the declared policy, then compute one summary row per group with n, missing, mean, SE and interval endpoints. Use that same summary table for ggplot2 error bars and Plotly error_y, keeping raw observations in separate layers/traces. Validate counts and coordinates, print the table and exactly two figures, and report remaining browser checks.

worked_examples.title: Compute the eligibility and uncertainty ledger
worked_examples.code:
d <- data.frame(id = c(paste0("A", 1:5), paste0("B", 1:5)), group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5), value = c(1, 2, 3, 4, NA_real_, 2, 3, 6, 7, NA_real_))
summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d$value, d$group), function(values) {
  observed <- values[!is.na(values)]
  n <- length(observed); se <- sd(observed) / sqrt(n); half <- qt(0.975, n - 1) * se
  data.frame(n = n, missing = sum(is.na(values)), mean = mean(observed), se = se, half = half)
}))
summary$group <- rownames(summary)
stopifnot(sum(summary$n) == 8, sum(summary$missing) == 2, max(abs(summary$mean - c(2.5, 4.5))) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(max(abs(summary$se^2 - c(5 / 12, 17 / 12))) < 1e-12)
print(summary)
worked_examples.explanation: The table retains both observed and missing counts and labels the mean-interval construction. These are the exact values later supplied to both rendering systems.
worked_examples.expected: Eight observed values, two missing values, group means 2.5/4.5 and squared SEs 5/12 and 17/12.

worked_examples.title: Represent summaries without double-counting observations
worked_examples.code:
summary <- data.frame(group = c("A", "B"), n = c(4L, 4L), mean = c(2.5, 4.5), se = sqrt(c(5 / 12, 17 / 12)))
summary$half <- qt(0.975, 3) * summary$se
p <- plotly::plot_ly(summary, x = ~group, y = ~mean, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = "Group mean", error_y = list(type = "data", array = summary$half, visible = TRUE))
p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Group"), yaxis = list(title = "Mean and 95% t interval"))
trace <- plotly::plotly_build(p)$x$data[[1]]
stopifnot(length(trace$x) == 2, max(abs(as.numeric(trace$y) - summary$mean)) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(trace$error_y$array) - summary$half)) < 1e-12)
print(summary)
print(p)
worked_examples.explanation: Two summary marks represent eight observations. The error bars reuse the declared half-widths; their visual presence does not change the observation denominator.
worked_examples.expected: Two mean marks with exact supplied t-interval half-widths.

reference:
d <- data.frame(id = c(paste0("A", 1:5), paste0("B", 1:5)), group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5), value = c(1, 2, 3, 4, NA_real_, 2, 3, 6, 7, NA_real_)) observed <- d[!is.na(d$value), ] summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d$value, d$group), function(values) { x <- values[!is.na(values)]; n <- length(x); se <- sd(x) / sqrt(n); half <- qt(0.975, n - 1) * se data.frame(n = n, missing = sum(is.na(values)), mean = mean(x), se = se, lower = mean(x) - half, upper = mean(x) + half, half = half) })) summary$group <- rownames(summary) stopifnot(nrow(d) == 10, nrow(observed) == 8, sum(summary$missing) == 2, !anyDuplicated(observed$id)) stopifnot(max(abs(summary$mean - c(2.5, 4.5))) < 1e-12, max(abs(summary$se^2 - c(5 / 12, 17 / 12))) < 1e-12) static <- ggplot2::ggplot(observed, ggplot2::aes(group, value)) + ggplot2::geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 2) + ggplot2::geom_errorbar(data = summary, mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = group, ymin = lower, ymax = upper), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.15) + ggplot2::geom_point(data = summary, mapping = ggplot2::aes(group, mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 4, size = 4) + ggplot2::labs(x = "Group", y = "Observed value and mean interval", caption = "Intervals: 95% Student t intervals for group means; synthetic independent-observation model") layers <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(static)$data stopifnot(nrow(layers[[1]]) == 8, nrow(layers[[2]]) == 2, nrow(layers[[3]]) == 2) interactive <- plotly::plot_ly() interactive <- plotly::add_trace(interactive, data = observed, x = ~group, y = ~value, customdata = ~id, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = "Observed", hovertemplate = "ID: %{customdata}
Group: %{x}
Value: %{y}Observed") interactive <- plotly::add_trace(interactive, data = summary, x = ~group, y = ~mean, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = "Mean and 95% t interval", inherit = FALSE, error_y = list(type = "data", array = summary$half, visible = TRUE)) interactive <- plotly::layout(interactive, xaxis = list(title = "Group"), yaxis = list(title = "Observed value and mean interval")) traces <- plotly::plotly_build(interactive)$x$data stopifnot(length(traces) == 2, length(traces[[1]]$x) == 8, length(traces[[2]]$x) == 2) stopifnot(identical(sort(as.character(traces[[1]]$customdata)), sort(observed$id))) stopifnot(max(abs(as.numeric(traces[[2]]$error_y$array) - summary$half)) < 1e-12) stopifnot(diff(summary$mean) == 2) print(summary) print(static) print(interactive) cat("r-060 reference checks passed\n")
solution_explanation:
The reference calculates one eligibility/summary table and uses it consistently across the static and interactive views. It checks raw IDs, layer counts, trace counts and uncertainty coordinates, preventing duplicated summary marks from being mistaken for additional observations.

The two printed figures share a numerical contract while retaining different rendering systems. The source and worker capture can establish actual PNG/Plotly payload production, but final browser usability remains a separate observation. The group difference is explicitly descriptive because the fixture supplies no causal assignment design.
